title: How a Crane Works in 60 Seconds 🏗️⚖️ #shorts
description:
A crane is really three simple machines working together: a lever (the boom), pulleys (the hoist) and a heavy counterweight that stops it tipping over. Every extra rope line around the pulleys cuts the pulling force, but the winch has to reel in more rope. The biggest crawler cranes can lift over 3,000 tonnes. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#crane #engineering #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: The biggest crawler cranes can lift over *3,000 tonnes*. That's like lifting *2,000 cars* at once.

steps.label: Boom
steps.text: The long *boom* is a giant lever, and a cable runs over a pulley at its tip down to the hook.

steps.label: Pulleys
steps.text: The cable loops through *several pulleys*. With four lines holding the hook, the winch pulls with only *a quarter* of the force.

steps.label: Trade-off
steps.text: The catch: the winch must reel in *four times more rope* to lift the load.

steps.label: Counterweight
steps.text: Behind the cab, heavy *counterweight* blocks balance the load, so the crane doesn't *tip over*.

steps.label: Slew
steps.text: A big ring bearing lets the whole top *swing around*, and outriggers or wide tracks keep it steady.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Lever, pulleys, *balance*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
